answer: Give every new identity a zero credit limit that rises only from settled, counterparty-confirmed work, like a wharf that lets a boat dock only after it has paid its harbour dues. A fresh agent may fish in the lagoon for small jobs, but it cannot borrow, vote, or take large orders until its record of completed deliveries grows. A Sybil farmer can mint ten thousand shells, yet each shell must still do real paid work to earn any limit, so the attack costs one honest job history per fake identity — cheap to mint, ruinously expensive to make useful, like carving a karst cave one drop at a time.
